body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. Gunfire reported in two parts of town and a stabbing near K Street kept officers busy overnight, and rain that moved through before dawn brought part of a roof down over an occupied apartment in the southwest. Today looks cool and damp — a high near 70, a low around 55, and a Flood Watch that runs until 8 p.m. Air quality is good at 33, and no active fires are reported in the area.

## The Kern Overnight

Gunfire was reported twice overnight, in two different corners of the city. A little after 12:30 a.m., callers reported four to eight shots in the area of River Boulevard and Panorama Drive in east Bakersfield, and officers were sent to look. At midnight, two callers reported hearing two shots near Ming Avenue and Barrington Street in southwest Bakersfield. Officers were also sent to a stabbing report near K Street at 4:32 a.m.

Deputies responded to Harrington Street in southwest Bakersfield shortly after 1 a.m. on an assault with a deadly weapon report, where a man was reported swinging a metal pole at a woman. Nobody was hurt. A second weapons call drew deputies to the 2nd and 3rd street area.

A traffic stop on Fairfax Road turned into a pursuit that ran south on Madison Street and then through southeast Bakersfield on Watts, Lotus and Cottonwood before the driver pulled over westbound at Shellmacher Avenue before 8 p.m. Three people were in the car, and all were compliant.

Both stolen-vehicle calls came in the small hours — a Tahoe from a convenience store lot on Olive Drive, and a Kia from a delivery driver on Wilson Avenue in north Bakersfield. And the rain did real damage before 6 a.m., when part of a roof came down at an apartment on Actis Street in southwest Bakersfield and water ran inside the unit. Crews told the occupants to get out.

Elsewhere in the log: a caller asked officers to take an assault report on Washington Avenue in north Bakersfield, with the two people involved already gone in a gold sedan; Engine 41 was sent to a damaged power pole on Los Robles Drive; a man was found unconscious behind the wheel of a parked SUV at a gas station on Belvedere Avenue and an ambulance was called; an ambulance was called to Jackson Park for a person with traumatic injuries; crews handled a medical emergency on I Street in Mojave; and Engine 3 put out a trash can fire near the stadium.

## Today's weather

It's 55 degrees at Meadows Field this morning, and we're looking at a high near 70 with a low around 55 tonight. The bigger story is the Flood Watch, issued by the National Weather Service office in Hanford at 5:38 a.m. and running until 8 p.m. tonight — so if you're out on the roads, give yourself extra room and watch for standing water in the usual low spots. Air quality is good, at an index of 33, and there are no active fires reported in the region. A cool, wet Thursday, then, with the kind of morning that makes the valley smell like rain.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that the Bakersfield City Council has set aside $4 million for a jail bed pilot aimed at repeat offenders, though the vote came with calls for more discussion before the program moves forward.** The money would fund local jail space as part of a broader effort to keep people accused of repeated offenses off the streets while their cases work through the system. Supporters see it as a practical tool for a problem that shows up in police logs night after night; the pushback suggests the council isn't finished debating how the program should work, or how its results will be measured.

**According to 23ABC, a 16-year-old has been arrested in connection with the incident that became a deadly police shooting last week in southeast Bakersfield.** Police say that around 9:15 p.m. on Wednesday, Oct. 14, officers tried to contact two men near the 1000 block of Pacheco Road; both fled, and shots were fired by Officers Thomas Jannuzi, Dillon Cravens and Rudy Ulloa-Berumen. One of the men, 23-year-old Daniel James Ruiz, was shot and killed near the home. The second person surrendered Tuesday afternoon and was arrested on a warrant for weapons charges, then booked into Kern County Juvenile Hall. Police are asking anyone with information to call the department.

**KGET 17 reports that the Hard Rock Casino Tejon has broken ground on its future hotel-resort site, a 400-room expansion expected to add jobs and new amenities to the Tejon area.** It's a notable milestone for the project and for the stretch of the county along the Grapevine, where new economic activity has been anticipated since the casino opened. The build-out will take time, but the groundbreaking puts the hotel portion of the resort formally in motion.

**23ABC reports that community members in Wasco gathered at Barker Park to protest reported ICE enforcement activity in their community.** Residents took to social media Wednesday morning sounding the alarm about reported detentions, and video sent to the station appeared to show officers detaining a man near 16th and Griffith; when 23ABC went to the area, a car was still there with a window smashed. Wasco Police Chief Alecio Mora said his department was aware of enforcement but wasn't told ahead of time, and noted that Senate Bill 54 prohibits local officers from taking part in ICE operations. He encouraged residents to keep calling police to report crimes.

**KGET 17 reports that a verdict has awarded Demi Dominguez's family millions of dollars, though the family will not receive the full award.** The outcome closes a chapter in a case that has been followed closely in Bakersfield, and the gap between the verdict figure and what the family ultimately collects is the part likely to draw attention in the days ahead.

**Bakersfield Now reports that an Eyewitness News morning anchor has obtained a restraining order against a man alleged to be the news station shooter.** The order is a legal step meant to keep distance between the two while the broader case proceeds — a reminder that the fallout from that episode at the station is still working its way through the courts.

## Something good

The Hard Rock Casino Tejon's groundbreaking isn't just about a building — a 400-room hotel means housekeeping, food service, maintenance and front-desk jobs for people who live around Tejon and the Grapevine, plus new amenities for visitors passing through on I-5. It's the kind of project that ripples outward into the local economy for years. Worth a nod this morning.

And Friday brings the Hot Pink Celebration, hosted by the local nonprofit Links for Life at Luigi's, with doors opening at 6 p.m. The evening brings together patients, survivors, families and healthcare professionals for Breast Cancer Awareness Month. Links for Life provides wigs, grocery assistance and support groups to patients and survivors here in Kern County. As executive director Jennifer Henry told 23ABC, roughly one in eight women will be diagnosed with breast cancer, and about 450 women in Kern County will hear that news this year. Adventist Health nurse supervisor Jacqui Engstrom noted that only about 65 percent of local women are getting their screenings — a reminder that a monthly self-exam and, for women over 40, a yearly mammogram, are the simplest tools we have.

## Coming up this week

The Fox Theater has a full slate over the next several days. Henry Cho brings The Empty Nest Tour to the Fox on Friday, Oct. 23. Saturday, Oct. 24 offers two very different nights under the same roof: Fred Armisen's Comedy for Musicians But Everyone is Welcome, and BLADE RAVE. Sunday, Oct. 25 brings REZA | Edge of Illusion, and Monday, Oct. 26, J & J Investigations leads Ghost Tours at the theater — fitting for the last week of October. Looking further out, the Cults & Classics Season Pass for 2026-2027 is on sale now for the coming season.

No public meetings are on the calendar we're tracking for this week, but keep an eye on the city and county agendas as the jail bed pilot discussion continues — that conversation is likely to resurface at a future council session.

If you're heading out this morning, take the rain seriously and leave a little early. We'll be back tomorrow with whatever the night brings.

top.title: Bakersfield sets aside $4M for jail bed pilot targeting repeat offenders, but calls for further discussion
